title: JavaScript Browser Environment Applied Check
description: Test your ability to diagnose practical browser JavaScript issues involving DOM selection, element updates, events, script loading, storage, navigation, security boundaries, rendering, compatibility, and DevTools.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt:
What is the likely problem?
```html
<head>
  <script src="app.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <button id="save">Save</button>
</body>
```
```js
const button = document.querySelector("#save");
button.addEventListener("click", save);
```

options.text: The script may run before the button exists in the DOM
Event listeners only work inside CSS files

questions.explanation: A blocking script in the head can run before the body is parsed. Use `defer`, move the script, or wait for `DOMContentLoaded`.

options.text: Check that `status` exists before using it

questions.explanation: `querySelector()` can return `null`, so code should handle that when the element might be absent.

questions.prompt:
What is the main security issue here?
```js
comments.innerHTML = userComment;
```

options.text: Untrusted content is parsed as HTML, which can create an XSS risk
Comments cannot be displayed in the DOM
The browser will automatically delete the page title

questions.explanation: `innerHTML` parses strings as HTML. Use `textContent` for untrusted plain text.

questions.prompt: Which code correctly stores and reads an object in `localStorage`?
questions.explanation: Web storage stores strings, so objects should be stringified and parsed with JSON.

options.text: It uses event delegation, so buttons added later can still be handled
It prevents all clicks from bubbling
It stores every task in cookies automatically

questions.explanation: A listener on the parent can handle events from current and future child buttons because click events bubble.

options.text: The two arrow functions are different function objects

questions.explanation: To remove a listener, pass the same function reference that was used when adding it.

questions.prompt: Which script loading choice is best for two dependent classic scripts that should not block HTML parsing?

options.text: Use `defer` on both scripts in dependency order

questions.explanation: `defer` avoids blocking parsing and preserves execution order. `async` does not guarantee order.

questions.prompt:
What is the likely issue with this browser API code?
```js
await navigator.clipboard.writeText("Copied");
```

options.text: The Clipboard API may be unavailable or may reject, so feature detection and error handling are needed
`await` cannot be used with browser APIs

questions.explanation: Some browser APIs depend on support, permissions, secure context, or user activation. They can fail.

questions.prompt: Which URL-building code safely handles spaces and special characters in the query value?

options.text: `const params = new URLSearchParams({ q: search.value }); const url = `/search?${params}`;`
`const url = "/search?q=" + search.value;` is always safe for all input

questions.prompt:
What is the best reason to avoid this frontend code?
```js
const API_SECRET = "secret-value";
```

options.text: Frontend JavaScript is visible to users, so secrets can be exposed
Browser code cannot make network requests
Secrets can only be stored in CSS classes

questions.explanation: Secrets should not be shipped to the browser. Use a backend for secret-protected operations.

options.text: It mixes layout reads and writes repeatedly, which can hurt rendering performance
Template literals cannot be used with styles

questions.explanation: Reading layout and writing styles in a loop can force repeated layout work. Batch reads and writes when performance matters.

questions.prompt: A `fetch()` request appears to fail. Which DevTools panel should you check first to inspect status, headers, response, timing, and CORS messages?
questions.explanation: The Network panel shows the browser's HTTP requests and responses, which is essential for debugging fetch issues.

options.text: A user-controlled `next` value may send users to an attacker-controlled site

questions.explanation: Redirect targets should be validated, commonly by allowing only trusted origins or relative paths.

questions.prompt: What should you do before relying on a newer browser API in production code?

options.text: Check support with feature detection and provide a fallback or alternate path when needed
Assume all browsers support all APIs equally
Store the API name in a cookie

questions.explanation: Feature detection and fallback behavior make browser code more reliable across different browser versions.

options.text: The attribute may still show the original HTML value, while the property shows the current form value
Inputs cannot be changed after page load

questions.explanation: Attributes and properties are related but not always the same. Use properties like `value` and `checked` for current form state.
